title: Array Nesting
statement: `nums` holds every integer from `0` to `n - 1` exactly once, where `n` is its length. For a starting index `k`, form the chain `nums[k]`, `nums[nums[k]]`, `nums[nums[nums[k]]]`, ..., always using the latest value as the next index, and end the chain just before a value would appear in it for the second time. Return the greatest number of values any such chain can contain, over all starting indices `k`.
constraints: All values of nums are distinct
notes:
## Intuition

Because `nums` is a permutation, following `i -> nums[i]` from any index walks around a cycle and returns to where it began. The values in that cycle are exactly the chain for any start inside it, so every index on the same cycle gives the same length. The brute force walks the chain from every index with a set, which is O(n²) in the worst case. Instead, measure each cycle once and mark its slots so no later start walks it again.

## Approach

1. Keep `longest = 0`.
2. For each `start`, walk from `current = start` while `nums[current]` is not the marker `-1`.
3. At each step read `next = nums[current]`, overwrite `nums[current]` with `-1`, move to `next` and add one to `length`.
4. When the walk lands on a marked slot the cycle is finished (or was already counted, giving `length = 0`); update `longest`.
5. Return `longest`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [5, 4, 0, 3, 1, 6, 2]`. From `start = 0`: visit 0 -> 5 -> 6 -> 2 and back to 0, marking four slots, so `length = 4`. `start = 1`: 1 -> 4 -> 1 gives 2. `start = 2` is marked, so its length is 0. `start = 3` points to itself, giving 1. Every remaining start is already marked. The answer is `4`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): each slot is marked once and a marked slot stops every later walk immediately.
- Space: O(1): the marks live inside `nums` itself.

## Pitfalls

- Save `nums[current]` in `next` before overwriting it, or the walk loses its way.
- Pick a marker that can never be a real value; `-1` is safe because every value is at least 0.
- Do not reset marks between starts: re-walking a cycle is what makes the naive version quadratic.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `longest` | longest cycle length found so far |
| `start` | index where the current walk begins |
| `current` | index being visited on the walk |
| `next` | value stored at `current`, the next index to visit |
| `length` | number of slots marked on this walk |

narration.2: No chain has been measured yet, so the longest length starts at zero.
narration.4: Try every index as the start of a walk.
narration.5: Count how many new slots this walk marks.
narration.6: The walk begins at the starting index.
narration.7: Keep walking until we reach a slot that is already marked, which closes the cycle.
narration.8: Remember where this slot points before we overwrite it.
narration.9: Mark the slot as visited so no later walk counts this cycle again.
narration.10: Jump to the index this slot pointed to.
narration.11: One more value belongs to this chain.
narration.13: The walk covered a whole cycle (or nothing, if it was already counted); keep the larger length.
narration.15: Every cycle was measured once; return the longest.
